title: Fabric on-demand billing and Zero-provisioned (F0) Capacity (Preview)
author: MonicaBoris

content.text:
Microsoft is introducing a new way to consume Fabric called on-demand billing. This includes a new F0 SKU, enabling customers to get started with zero upfront commitment, as well as a hybrid option that pairs any traditional F SKU with the flexibility of on-demand billing.
In addition to the traditional Fabric capacity model, customers can selectively enable on-demand billing for individual Fabric workloads, such as Data Factory or Data Warehouse, which are broken down into what is known as on-demand billing categories. Customers can set usage thresholds per billing category to maintain predictable governance and spend controls.
Ultimately, this gives organizations the flexibility to start with less upfront commitment, adapt to less predictable demand, and balance spiky or outsized workload needs alongside more predictable and contained ones – providing more flexibility in how to consume, manage, and scale usage of Fabric.
Flexible capacity models
Fabric supports multiple capacity options to match different project stages and needs:
• Start with F0. F0 is a zero-provisioned capacity SKU with no upfront compute-capacity charge. With this approach, Fabric workloads (billing categories) exclusively use on-demand billing - which can help with evaluation, development / early launch stages, or workloads whose capacity needs are not yet predictable.
• Add on-demand billing to an F2 or higher capacity. Using SKUs customers have today, they can move Fabric workload(s) of their choice outside of the limits of their shared F-SKU capacity and pay for them separately. All other workloads continue using the provisioned F SKU capacity, making this a practical option where some Fabric workload needs are stable while others are bursty or outsized.
• Traditional F SKU. This is Fabric’s traditional model where customers can select a capacity size ranging from F2 to F8192 based on their needs. This option remains in-tact alongside the two new ways to consume Fabric outlined above.
How on-demand billing works
On-demand billing is managed for supported Fabric workloads at the billing category level, ensuring consistent behavior across all workspaces within a capacity. Each category is billed based on actual usage, allowing workloads to scale independently depending on demand. Unlike workloads running from a fixed capacity SKU, on-demand usage is unsmoothed.
Capacity administrators can enable on-demand billing for a category from the On-demand billing section on the capacity’s Details tab.
Feature: Enable On-demand billing for a category.
On-demand consumption is measured in CU-hours (without smoothing). Pricing is based on a multiplier of the pay-as-you-go CU price for any given region, and it varies by billing category from 1x to 3X pay-as-you-go. Storage charges remain separate from compute charges.
Note: Autoscale billing for Apache Spark, now re-named “On-demand billing for Apache Spark,” remains generally available and functions as before. Pricing remains unchanged.
Example usage scenario
An organization running Data Warehouse and Data Factory workloads on a Fabric capacity may choose to place the Data Warehouse category on on-demand billing during a seasonal promotion. Compute intensive Warehouse queries could scale independently while steady workloads continue using the provisioned capacity, without the need for capacity expansion. When demand settles, the administrator can return the category to the shared-capacity model, balancing performance needs with cost efficiency.
Spend controls and governance
To support cost predictability, administrators can configure spend limits using CU-hours over a rolling 24-hour window. When the limit is reached:
• New operations are temporarily paused
• In-flight operations continue until completion
• Billing resumes automatically once the window resets
This provides a safety mechanism for preventing unexpected usage spikes while preserving system stability.
Feature: Configure the spend limit for an on-demand billing category.
Monitoring on-demand consumption
On-demand billing consumption can be monitored using the Capacity Metrics App, in the new “On-demand compute” tab, on a per billing category basis.
Feature: Inspect on-demand usage in Capacity Metrics App.
Why this matters
These updates introduce a more flexible approach to capacity management in Fabric:
• Lower entry barriers without upfront commitment with F0.
• Improved cost efficiency by paying only for usage in burst-heavy workloads.
• Better workload isolation between steady and variable compute patterns.
• Stronger governance controls through category-level billing and spend limits.
Together, these capabilities help organizations modernize infrastructure without over-provisioning capacity or sacrificing control.
Learn more
For additional details, refer to the Microsoft Fabric documentation on on-demand billing and capacity management.
